provenance: Step 1.2 of the block-automation rebuild (issue #316): in wrap mode (profile key entry_hist) the forward pass keeps a join history as one hidden zesu_join_history group, aligns the history groups of edges that bypass a loop, keeps the disjunction of incoming edge guards, names call-record binders with the call prefix, states the slice window of a call at its return site, and writes a store that covers a packaged array as the stored bytes. Without the profile key the legacy render is byte-identical (checked for nextUint64 and decodeParentHeader).
statement: Source evaluation does not establish any generated contract or predecessor entailment.
limitations: A load inside an owned uninitialized span (`↦ₘ?`, Islaris' per-byte ∃ v : bv 8) reads fresh existential bytes with no facts; an unowned or out-of-extent uninitialized byte stays unknown.

A jump at a CFG return site leaves the function as a function_return exit; a jump from a CFG tail-call instruction to its callee leaves it as a tail_call exit; any other unknown target stops the path.

An address that carries an owned array base and a symbolic addend reads that array as a list lookup; its index range (below the actual array length) is a path condition and an open read obligation; an array without a length term stops the read. A store at a symbolic index has an owner only when one initialized owned array base is its addend and every other memory resource is disjoint from that array; its index range is an open obligation.
A call ends its block; its return site is a cut that continues only from a call-return seed (call_boundary.call_return_seed). Loop cuts require source-bound inputs.
